## The pitch

A diffusion model turns **pure static into an image**. It does exactly one
thing, about a thousand times:

::: {style="text-align:center"}
[subtract a *little* noise, correctly.]{.big}
:::

::: {.note}
Everything in this deck is computed **exactly** — no neural network anywhere.
The demos are on the course site.
:::

## Our dataset: two points

Samples from an unknown distribution; task: **produce more of the same**. Today:

$$p_{\text{data}} \;=\; \tfrac12 \delta_{-1} \;+\; \tfrac12 \delta_{+1}$$

- Generating = flipping a coin — *that is why it is the right dataset:* nothing can hide
- You already know one generative model: fit $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ by MLE, then sample
- **Module 1:** MLE $=$ minimizing $\mathrm{KL}(p_{\text{data}} \,\|\, p_\theta)$

## Why images break the direct approach

- A $64\times64$ RGB image lives in a space with $256^{12288}$ configurations
- Almost all of them are **static** — random pixels never make a face
- Real data is a vanishingly thin filament of the space

::: {.note}
Writing down $p_\theta(\text{image})$ and fitting it directly is hopeless — the
curse of dimensionality (Module 1).
:::

## The diffusion idea

$$x_\sigma \;=\; x_0 + \sigma z, \qquad z \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1) \ \text{independent of } x_0$$

- Destroying structure with noise: **easy, fully understood**
- It always ends somewhere known — a Gaussian
- Then learn to walk **backwards**

## Watch noise accumulate

One point at $0$, kicked $k$ times by noise of size $\delta$: spread $=\delta\sqrt{k}$.
Any kick distribution → same Gaussian (CLT).

```{=html}
<iframe src="one-point-noise-demo.html" style="width:100%;height:60%;border:1px solid #cfdcec;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy" title="Progressively adding noise demo"></iframe>
```

## Forward: noise melts the two points

$$p_\sigma(x) = \tfrac12 \mathcal{N}(x; -1, \sigma^2) + \tfrac12 \mathcal{N}(x; +1, \sigma^2),
\qquad \operatorname{Var}(x_\sigma) = 1 + \sigma^2$$

- Two spikes → two bumps → one bell
- By $\sigma \approx 3$, indistinguishable in practice from $\mathcal{N}(0, 1+\sigma^2)$

::: {style="text-align:center"}
[Structure destroyed. Destination known.]{.big}
:::

## The inverse problem

You observe a noisy $x$. What was the clean point? Best guess under squared
error is the **posterior mean** $\mathbb{E}[x_0 \mid x_\sigma = x]$.

For the two-point prior, Bayes' rule gives it in closed form:

$$\mathbb{P}(x_0 = +1 \mid x) \;=\; \operatorname{sigmoid}\!\left(\frac{2x}{\sigma^2}\right)$$

::: {.note}
One line of algebra — **Exercise 1**, do it tonight.
:::

## The punchline

::: {style="text-align:center;border:3px solid #003f87;border-radius:10px;padding:.3em .5em;margin:.3em 0"}
$$\mathbb{E}[x_0 \mid x_\sigma = x] \;=\; \tanh\!\left(\frac{x}{\sigma^2}\right)$$
:::

- The optimal denoiser is a **tanh** — produced by nothing but probability
- $\sigma \to 0$: hard threshold — snap to the nearer point
- $\sigma \to \infty$: shrink to $0$ — trust the prior, not the observation

## Denoising = knowing the score

Differentiate $\log p_\sigma$ and compare — **Tweedie's formula**:

$$\mathbb{E}[x_0 \mid x] \;=\; x + \sigma^2\, \nabla_x \log p_\sigma(x)$$

- The **score** $\nabla_x \log p_\sigma$ points toward where noised data is denser
- Denoising and score estimation are the *same problem* — the hinge of Modules 3–4

## Run the diffusion backwards

Anneal $\sigma$ downward on a grid, nudging along the score:

$$y \;\leftarrow\; y + \frac{\sigma_k^2 - \sigma_{k+1}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{\tanh(y/\sigma_k^2) - y}{\sigma_k^2}$$

```{=html}
<iframe src="two-point-diffusion-demo.html" style="width:100%;height:52%;border:1px solid #cfdcec;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy" title="Two-point diffusion demo"></iframe>
```

## What you just saw

- Particles start as pure noise
- The cloud splits, condenses, lands on the two data points
- **Generation — with every step computed exactly, no neural network**

[The whole pipeline: noise the data → learn to denoise → run it backwards.]{.big}

## So where do neural networks come in?

For images, $\mathbb{E}[x_0 \mid x]$ has **no usable formula**. The network's
only job:

$$\text{approximate}\quad (x,\sigma) \;\mapsto\; \mathbb{E}[x_0 \mid x]$$

— to be the tanh we can no longer derive. Everything else survives unchanged.
